title: WorkBench C6 vs C0
h1: No detectable completion gap between C0 and C6
lede: On 90 WorkBench tasks, the all-English agent completed 73 and the Bangla agent (Bangla task and system prompt, replies forced to Bangla) 74. The difference, +1.1 points (95% CI −7.8 to +10.0), shows no detectable difference, and no Bangla failure was labelled primarily multilingual (single model annotator).
disc_note: The note under each card explains the failed run.
findings: No detectable completion gap: 81.1% English vs 82.2% Bangla, exact McNemar p = 1.00. The 95% CI lower bound is −7.8 pp (task sampling only; run-to-run noise not measured).

The disagreements show no detectable difference and no clear language cause (no repeat runs yet, so noise is not measured): 7 tasks only English solved, 8 only Bangla solved, and the failed side was labelled reasoning in 12 of the 15.
Harmful side effects were lower in Bangla (8.9% vs 16.7%), but the CI reaches zero (−15.6 to +0.0 points). 8 of 16 Bangla failures leave no side effect, against 2 of 17 English failures.
Failure mix is similar: reasoning 11 vs 10, planning 4 vs 2, tool use 1 vs 2, control flow 1 vs 2 (English vs Bangla). 0 of 16 Bangla failures have multilingual as the primary label.
Analytics is the one domain where Bangla is lower (87% vs 67%; 3 tasks only English solved, none only Bangla). With 15 tasks per domain this is descriptive only.
Multi-domain tasks are still the hard part (53% and 60%), with calendar free-slot errors as the main shared weak spot in both languages.
threats: English ran on 2026-10-04 and Bangla on 2026-10-05, so provider drift is possible. There is no English repeat yet, so the noise floor is not measured.
The Bangla system prompt translation, and the task translations, have not been reviewed by a native speaker. If they change, the Bangla side must be re-run.
One model (gemma4:31b, Gemma family, trained heavily on multilingual data). Models with weaker Bangla may behave differently.
Small sample: n = 90, 15 per domain. Per-domain differences are descriptive only.
C6 changes the task, the system prompt and the reply language together, so a difference could not be assigned to one of them.
Single run per task at temperature 0 on a hosted free-tier endpoint.
Failure labels were assigned by one model annotator, not by human annotators.
language_scan: 88 of 88 non-empty Bangla answers are in Bangla; none switched to English. English appeared only as borrowed names, titles and status values.
51 of 88 answers write numbers in Bengali digits (366 digits), but every tool argument uses ASCII digits. 0 of 285 tool calls passed Bangla script as an argument.
One invalid tool name in Bangla (crm:77, customer_relationship_manager_update_task), none in English.

2–3 of the 7 Bangla-only failures are relative-date errors (email:41, analytics:119, md:120), against 0 of 8 English-only failures. analytics:98 is not counted: it resolved the weekday correctly and erred on the baseline day. This grouping is post hoc, so it is a hypothesis for repeated runs.

আগামী শুক্রবার ("next Friday") was read as the coming Friday (Dec 1) in md:120, where the answer key expects Dec 8. It stays labelled reasoning, but it may be a translation-fidelity issue: the same phrase gave Dec 8 in md:169. It goes to the native-speaker review.
Observation: 2 of 90 Bangla runs (crm:74, md:149) ended with an empty final answer; English had 0. The traces show no cause.
